Jakkalsjagter

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Farmers are resorting to hunting Jackals in the Northern Cape to protect their dwindling sheep numbers

Unique Selling Point:
Seven years of drought means that most sheep farmers are down to 30% of their livestock carrying capacity in the Northern Cape. Even with recent rains it will take years for livestock numbers to recover and farmers are desperate. But the one animal that was not so much affected by the drought is the Jackal. Over the past decade their numbers have exploded and with a lack of apex predators keeping them in check, and the fact that food is still in abundance, the livestock farmers are suffering. For years many farmers have resorted to taking out jackals, calling them vermin and pests. There are even hunters specialising in Jackals. They are hired to take out entire families of Jackals to protect farmers' livelihoods. We have been invited to accompany a Jackal hunt and see the problem facing the farmers, first hand.

Summary:
Human-Carnivore conflict is nothing new, but it is escalating across the continent as wild habitats decrease and human encroaching increases. Many Environmental NGO's run programmes, working with farmers when it comes to predator control. Various non-lethal deterrent methods exist, but in the forgotten areas of the Northern Cape - Namaqualand, farmers are faced with many problems. Electrified fencing, and even so-called Jackal proof mesh fencing is expensive and many cannot afford this. Jackals are clever and learn to dodge poison collars and dogs. There are even programmes that encourages farmers to play music, or ultra sonic sounds to keep predators away. Farmers will tell you that these are costly and largely ineffective. Many farmers choose to hunt Jackals - either themselves or they hire a professional to do the job.

Further information:
There is very little you can farm with along the West Coast. Traditionally this has been sheep farming areas for many generations. With the drive to draw tourism to Namaqualand and the West Coast (Diamond Route) conservation areas are being expanded and the buffer zones that used to exist between wildlife and farmers are no more. Fences have been dropped and now every farm is a McDonalds for the Jackals and their numbers have exploded.

Danie Du Plooy hunted Jackals for over 20 years. recently retired, he moved to Olifantshoek, but he has kept his records. it was his mission to understand Jackals, how they breed and their hunting and feeding habits. He says that hunting lone jackals have very little value, since another family will simply move into the territory, or the pups will simply grow and take over the area... To have any real effect, entire families need to be taken out and it's not easy to shoot a Jackal pup.

Farmer Willie van Dyk farms with Sheep just outside Kleinzee on the West Coast. He put up electric fencing at a huge cost, but it only helped for a while. Soon the Jackals learned to dig under the fence and the stock losses continued. Fed up, he decided to start hunting Jackals and will take us on a hunt...

Van Dyk's neighbour was so despondent about his losses that he sold his sheep, opting for goats.he believed that goats are not on the Jackal menu. He was wrong. Last week Jackals caught and ate 7 of his goats in one evening!

As far back as 1922, the jackal was declared a pest, and an “evil to be reckoned with”. (According to the Journal of the Dept of Agriculture - Sept 1922). Black-backed jackal were controlled intensely with over 350 000 animals reportedly killed in the Cape Province from 1889 - 1908…

In the past, the South African government subsidised farmers with predator control methods which mostly included lethal control such as the use of indiscriminate traps. This had very little negative effect on black-backed jackal populations, but a potential increased loss of other mammalian species (non-target species) and biodiversity has been observed on farmlands. But, since the 1990’s government no longer supports the control of Jackals and since the mid-2010’s farmers have been reporting an increase in Jackal numbers and predation on their livestock. Additionally, other apex predators numbers have fallen. An abundance of lions and leopards would have helped to keep jackal numbers down…

Press Release:


In the Northern Cape jackals have very few natural enemies and a steady supply of food from the sheep farms across the province. But how do farmers keep their flocks safe, especially when the veld is lush and the jackal plentiful from the recent rain? Carte Blanche explores the controversial practice of varminting — hunting so-called problem animals on farms. While many see this as cruel and unnecessary, for the Jakkalsjagter it’s a matter of skill and pride as he maintains a last line of defence for some farmers..

Script:


JAKKALSJAGTER


DANIE
Ek jag al vandat ek op die plaas groot geword het in Transvaal, net voor Klerksdorp.

I’ve been hunting since I grew up on the farm
in Transvaal, just before Klerksdorp.


DANIE
So dit is, dit is maar ‘n passie!

So, it is a passion.
LINK
I’m in the middle of the Northern Cape, just outside a little town called Olifantshoek. Why here, you may ask… this is where I meet a legend… Oom Danie die Jakkalsjagter.
V/O
The name Danie du Plooy is known to farmers across the province - from Namaqualand to the heart of the Karoo… and even here on the edge of the Kalahari…
UPSOUND
“Oom Danie”
“Aangename kennis”

Pleased to meet you
V/O
Danie is a professional hunter, specialising in jackal, and other so-called problem animals on farms.
UPSOUND
I love his little camo van…
V/O
We’re spending the day with him… to get a glimpse of a world that we often ignore… And like most farm visits, it starts with a tour…


UPSOUND
Ek dink nie mens kan op ‘n plaas wees en nie groente hê nie.

Ja. Wat sal jy eet?

I don’t think one can be on a farm and not have vegetables.

Yes, what will you eat?
V/O
From the outset it is clear that Danie is a man of detail. Everything has its place.
DANIE
So what’s in this magic box?

Dis nou jou roepers, en die mondfluite en oorbeskerming en batterye…
This is your callers, the whistles, and ear protection and batteries..
V/O
His custom-made bakkie is kitted with everything he needs for a night out in the veld. That includes lots of warm clothes and a variety of lights.
DANIE
Baie belangrik is, jy moet altyd jou lense beskerm, want met die voertuig se ry dan krap jou ligte…

It is very important, you must always protect your lenses because with the vehicle moving you might scratch your lights and they are quite expensive.
UPSOUND
Al die vir ‘n jakkals?

Dit net vir ‘n jakkals…

All this for a jackal?
This is all just for a jackal.
V/O
Here in the Northern Cape, jackals have very few natural enemies and quite a lot of food… Even in the lean years when the veld is bare, farms provide a constant supply of succulent lamb pickings…
DANIE
But why do you hunt jackals?

Dit is maar vir genetiese druk, om hulle uit die veld uit te kry, om die plaasboer te help om sy produksielyn sterker te maak. ‘n Jakkals sal sommer in ‘n week se tyd hier drie vier skape vang…

It is to remove them from the veld. To help the farmer strengthen his production line.

A jackal will easily, within a week, catch three, four sheep.
V/O
It is estimated that in the Northern Cape one out of every ten lambs under the age of six months, will end up as a snack for a predator…
JOHANNES
Ongediertes, veral jakkalse, … jaarliks beloop my skade iets tussen R20,000 tot R40,000. En as jy die winsgrense inreken wat ‘n boer het, dan is dit ‘n geweldige probleem vir jou.

Vermin, especially jackal… annually my losses runs somewhere between R20 000 to R40 000.

And if you take into account the profit margins of a farmer, then it’s a huge problem.
V/O
Johannes Agenbach has been running the 3,600ha family farm between Olifantshoek and Kalaharigrens for the past five years. Keeping the jackals away from his sheep is complicated and costly.
JOHANNES
Ons kamp nie ons hele plase af teen jakkalse nie, ons identifiseer sekere kampe in ons plase en dan boer ons daar skaap, en dit wil ons beheer.

We don’t fence our entire farms against jackals.

We identify certain camps on our farms and then we farm our sheep there, and that we want to manage.


V/O
Where possible, camps are enclosed with jackal-proof, or, electric fencing, but the jackal always seems to find a way to get at the sheep.
JOHANNES
Ons skiet nou maar en ons kry professionele jakkalsjagters in om dit te doen want dit is vir ons die bekostigbaarste op die oomblik om dit so te doen.

We shoot them and we get professional jackal hunters to do it because that is for us the most affordable option at the moment to do it like this.
V/O
Varminting( pr. vaa-minting), or shooting what some people refer to as vermin - like jackal and caracal - is widely practiced on private farmland across South Africa… but not without controversy. For many it is cruel and unnecessary… But Danie takes pride in his craft..


DANIE
Mac: Do you try and do it in the most decent way, “Een skoot, dan is hy dood”, no pain?

Absoluut. Jy moet soek, jy moet identifiseer, jy moet weet waar jou skootplasing is en jy moet weet as jy die skoot trek is dit die regte keuse wat jy maak.

One shot then he is dead.

Absolutely. You must search, you must identify. You must know where your shot placement is and you must know when you pull the trigger it is the right decision that you make.


V/O
With the bakkie loaded, it’s time to make our way north. It’s 80 kilometres on a dirt road and the recent rain poses some challenges.

Danie wants to make sure we’re early, so that there’s ample time to calibrate his weapon.
DANIE
Jou toerusting moet reg wees. Jou skietvaardigheid moet baie baie goed wees.

Your equipment must be right.
Your shooting skills must be very good.
V/O
Hunting at night in lush veld like this, means there’s no room for error and he doesn’t want to disappoint his client.
DANIE
Dit is so lekker om vir die plaasboer te sê - of vir die ou vir wie jy jag - hierso meneer ek het jou twee jakkalse vir jou uitgeskiet. En dan is dit ook baie sleg partykere as jy nie die jakkalse kon kry nie om vir die man te sê maar kyk hier meneer ek is jammer ek kon hulle nie kry nie, hulle was te skelm, of ek het ‘n fout gemaak…

It is so good to say to the farmer - or the person you’re hunting for:
“Here you go, Sir. I shot your two jackals.”

And then it is also bad sometimes when you don’t find jackals, to tell the man: “Sir, I am sorry, I couldn’t find them. They were too sly, or I made a mistake.”
V/O
A sly or “skelm” jackal - as Danie calls it - is one that knows it is being hunted.
V/O
Injuring or even missing the jackal will make the next hunt so much more challenging…
DANIE
Ek het by ‘n oom, Jan Toon op Langplaas het ek vir amper twee jaar gesukkel met een jakkals wat ek drie keer misgeskiet het. Omdat sy elke keer op 4, 500 meter vir my net nie kans gee nie. En daai jakkals het vir my ore aangesit.

At Oom Jan Toon’s farm Langplaas, I struggled for almost two years with a jackal that I missed on three occasions, because every time, at 400, 500 metres she did not give me an opportunity. And that jackal taught me a lesson.

LINK
Farming is about a lot more than a love of the land. This is how farmers put food on the table and send their kids to school… and like most of us they’ll do whatever it takes to protect their livelihoods
JOHANNES
Ons wil nie hê die jakkals moet uitsterf nie, gladnie. Die jakkals het net soveel reg soos ek om hier te wees. Maar die jakkals moet in sy area wees en ek moet in my area wees. Sodat ons kan altwee lewe…

We don’t want the jackal to go extinct. Not at all. The jackal has just as much right as me to be here. But the jackal must stay in his area and I must be in my area, so that we can both live.

Mac: Have you tried any other methods to get rid of them?

Ja, ek het vir my anatoliese herdershonde gekry en dit werk relatief goed, en nou saans moet ek my skape op hok laat slaap, ek kan hulle nooit in die veld laat slaap nie.

Yes, I got Anatolian sheepdogs and that works relatively well, and then at night I must let my sheep sleep in an enclosure. I can never let them sleep in the veld.
V/O
And although some of these mitigation measures help, Johannes maintains there are simply too many jackals.
LINK
Jackals are not just a problem for farmers in Olifantshoek. Even here, 700kms away and in a totally different environment … same issues!
MEISIE
Ons kry nie geboer saam met die jakkalse nie. Ek sê sommer hulle vreet ons oes op.

We cannot farm with the jackals. I say, they eat our entire harvest.
V/O
Meisie and Danie Engelbrecht farm in Namaqualand…. With the expansion of conservation land to draw tourism to the area, they are struggling to cope with the thriving jackal population… and they are losing sheep on a weekly basis.
MEISIE
‘N Boer se hart kan daai nie hanteer nie. Dis baie erg. Met hierdie droogte jare, dis al inkomste wat ons het. Ons lammeroeste is minder want ons ooie het gevrek van die droogte en dan kom die jakkals en dan kom vang hy …ag manne met meer skape dis maklik sommer ‘n klomp in ‘n nag.

A farmer’s heart cannot handle that. It’s very bad. With these years of drought that is all the income we have. Our lamb harvests are less because our ewes died from the drought…
V/O
Here, herding the sheep to a kraal at night is not an option - the farm is just too vast and grazing too little…
MEISIE
Dan moet jy voer koop. Jy moet oor hierdie sleg pad met jou bakkie moet jy voer aanry van Springbok af wat peperduur is. Ons kan dit nie bekostig nie.

Then you must buy feed. On this bad road, with your bakkie, you must transport feed from Springbok, which is very expensive. We can’t afford that.
V/O
They also cannot afford the additional labour, or to electrify their fences…
MEISIE
Mac: So, hoe maak julle?

Hoe maak ons nou? Gee raad asseblief…

So, what do you do?

What should we do? Give advice, please.
V/O
Although Meisie says they do not kill the jackals on this farm, Danie the Jackal hunter has spent many nights on the West Coast plains …
DANIE
In die Weskus het ek normaalweg een elke drie aande geskiet - gemiddeld. En die meeste wat ek in een aand geskiet het was 7 jakkalse…

On the West Coast I normally shot one every three nights on average. And the most that I shot in one evening was seven jackals.
V/O
As the sun begins to draw water it is time for the final preparations…
DANIE
Ek het sommer ‘n mobile bord wat ek opstel met pale…

I have a mobile board that I put up with poles…
V/O
Danie uses a high caliber Winchester rifle with a telescope and rangefinder - specifically designed for varmint and big game.
DANIE

Mac: Gaan jy ons waarsky voor jy ‘n skoot vat.

Ek gaan. Defnitief.

Mac: Baie dankie

Hy Het darem ‘n silencer… so hy sal nie ‘n baie harde klap geluid maak nie…

Will you warn us before you take a shot?
I Will, definitely.
Thank you very much.
It does at least have a silencer, so it won't make a loud noise.
SHOT


V/O
(**Snigger) I was not quite as prepared for that, as I thought…
V/O
Satisfied with the calibration results, the rifle and lights are mounted on the vehicle…. And just as we set off, Johannes brings us a lamb carcass he just found near the road.
JOHANNES
Hierdie is ‘n extreme geval. Gewoonlik eet hy minder. Hier kan jy sien hy het tot sy ribbes regdeur afgebyt, sy bene uitgebreek. Alles opgevreet…

This is an extreme incident. Normally it eats less. Here you can see it even bit right through its ribs, broke the bones. Everything is eaten.
V/O
We set off to find the culprit, before it does more damage.
MAC UPSOUND
So the hunt is now seriously on. There’s a searchlight doing the rounds, and hoping that we might catch a jackal’s eyes.
DANIE
Okay - woaw!
Sit die rooi ligte af. Haal jou voet van die briek af…
UPSOUND
I can hear them…
SHOT


MAC
That sound was loud. And it just came out of nowhere. I think that was the scariest part of it all. When you’re sitting in pitch black darkness, in the middle of no-where and you just hear that shot…. My heart almost stopped…
DANIE
As jy ‘n jakkals geskiet het, jy kry satisfaksie. Dit is satisfaksie wat jy gee omdat jy jou werk reg gedoen het.

Hy het ‘n reg om te lewe. Hy het ‘n rego m te lewe want ons het in sy gebied ingetree met ons boerdery. Maar ongelukkig, in elke divisie van werk en sport is daar besering, en ongelukkig is die jakkals ‘n plaag. En ‘n probleem…

When you’ve shot a jackal you get satisfaction. It is satisfaction that you give because you did your job right.

It does have a right to live. It has a right to live because it is us who moved into his territory with our farming. But unfortunately, in every division of work and sport there is injury, and unfortunately jackal are a plague and a problem.




PROMO 1 11”
Across the Northern Cape, farmers are pitched against jackals in a battle to survive… Often hard choices have to be made but for some the answer is clear cut…




PROMO 2 21”
Hunting a jackal at 200 metres in the dead of night takes a sharp eye and a lot of patience.

UPSOUND: Trees, thick bush… and still spot a jackal’s eyes… nah!







PROMO 3 21”
Farmers and jackals compete for land… and livestock…

UPSOUND: ‘n Boer se hart kan daai nie hanteer nie. Dis baie erg.

For some there is only one way to stop the onslaught…

UPSOUND: Teen 3050 voet per sekond gee dit vir jou genoeg trefkrag om jou eerste skoot ‘n doodskoot te gee.

DANIE So dit is, dit is maar ‘n passie! So, it is a passion. LINK I’m in the middle of the Northern Cape, just outside a little town called Olifantshoek. Why here, you may ask… this is where I meet a legend… Oom Danie die Jakkalsjagter. V/O The name Danie du Plooy is known to farmers across the province - from Namaqualand to the heart of the Karoo… and even here on the edge of the Kalahari… UPSOUND “Oom Danie” “Aangename kennis” Pleased to meet you V/O Danie is a professional hunter, specialising in jackal, and other so-called problem animals on farms. UPSOUND I love his little camo van… V/O We’re spending the day with him… to get a glimpse of a world that we often ignore… And like most farm visits, it starts with a tour… UPSOUND Ek dink nie mens kan op ‘n plaas wees en nie groente hê nie. Ja. Wat sal jy eet? I don’t think one can be on a farm and not have vegetables. Yes, what will you eat? V/O From the outset it is clear that Danie is a man of detail. Everything has its place. DANIE So what’s in this magic box? Dis nou jou roepers, en die mondfluite en oorbeskerming en batterye… This is your callers, the whistles, and ear protection and batteries.. V/O His custom-made bakkie is kitted with everything he needs for a night out in the veld. That includes lots of warm clothes and a variety of lights. DANIE Baie belangrik is, jy moet altyd jou lense beskerm, want met die voertuig se ry dan krap jou ligte… It is very important, you must always protect your lenses because with the vehicle moving you might scratch your lights and they are quite expensive. UPSOUND Al die vir ‘n jakkals? Dit net vir ‘n jakkals… All this for a jackal? This is all just for a jackal. V/O Here in the Northern Cape, jackals have very few natural enemies and quite a lot of food… Even in the lean years when the veld is bare, farms provide a constant supply of succulent lamb pickings… DANIE But why do you hunt jackals? Dit is maar vir genetiese druk, om hulle uit die veld uit te kry, om die plaasboer te help om sy produksielyn sterker te maak. ‘n Jakkals sal sommer in ‘n week se tyd hier drie vier skape vang… It is to remove them from the veld. To help the farmer strengthen his production line. A jackal will easily, within a week, catch three, four sheep. V/O It is estimated that in the Northern Cape one out of every ten lambs under the age of six months, will end up as a snack for a predator… JOHANNES Ongediertes, veral jakkalse, … jaarliks beloop my skade iets tussen R20,000 tot R40,000. En as jy die winsgrense inreken wat ‘n boer het, dan is dit ‘n geweldige probleem vir jou. Vermin, especially jackal… annually my losses runs somewhere between R20 000 to R40 000. And if you take into account the profit margins of a farmer, then it’s a huge problem. V/O Johannes Agenbach has been running the 3,600ha family farm between Olifantshoek and Kalaharigrens for the past five years. Keeping the jackals away from his sheep is complicated and costly. JOHANNES Ons kamp nie ons hele plase af teen jakkalse nie, ons identifiseer sekere kampe in ons plase en dan boer ons daar skaap, en dit wil ons beheer. We don’t fence our entire farms against jackals. We identify certain camps on our farms and then we farm our sheep there, and that we want to manage. V/O Where possible, camps are enclosed with jackal-proof, or, electric fencing, but the jackal always seems to find a way to get at the sheep. JOHANNES Ons skiet nou maar en ons kry professionele jakkalsjagters in om dit te doen want dit is vir ons die bekostigbaarste op die oomblik om dit so te doen. We shoot them and we get professional jackal hunters to do it because that is for us the most affordable option at the moment to do it like this. V/O Varminting( pr. vaa-minting), or shooting what some people refer to as vermin - like jackal and caracal - is widely practiced on private farmland across South Africa… but not without controversy. For many it is cruel and unnecessary… But Danie takes pride in his craft.. DANIE Mac: Do you try and do it in the most decent way, “Een skoot, dan is hy dood”, no pain? Absoluut. Jy moet soek, jy moet identifiseer, jy moet weet waar jou skootplasing is en jy moet weet as jy die skoot trek is dit die regte keuse wat jy maak. One shot then he is dead. Absolutely. You must search, you must identify. You must know where your shot placement is and you must know when you pull the trigger it is the right decision that you make. V/O With the bakkie loaded, it’s time to make our way north. It’s 80 kilometres on a dirt road and the recent rain poses some challenges. Danie wants to make sure we’re early, so that there’s ample time to calibrate his weapon. DANIE Jou toerusting moet reg wees. Jou skietvaardigheid moet baie baie goed wees. Your equipment must be right. Your shooting skills must be very good. V/O Hunting at night in lush veld like this, means there’s no room for error and he doesn’t want to disappoint his client. DANIE Dit is so lekker om vir die plaasboer te sê - of vir die ou vir wie jy jag - hierso meneer ek het jou twee jakkalse vir jou uitgeskiet. En dan is dit ook baie sleg partykere as jy nie die jakkalse kon kry nie om vir die man te sê maar kyk hier meneer ek is jammer ek kon hulle nie kry nie, hulle was te skelm, of ek het ‘n fout gemaak… It is so good to say to the farmer - or the person you’re hunting for: “Here you go, Sir. I shot your two jackals.” And then it is also bad sometimes when you don’t find jackals, to tell the man: “Sir, I am sorry, I couldn’t find them. They were too sly, or I made a mistake.” V/O A sly or “skelm” jackal - as Danie calls it - is one that knows it is being hunted. V/O Injuring or even missing the jackal will make the next hunt so much more challenging… DANIE Ek het by ‘n oom, Jan Toon op Langplaas het ek vir amper twee jaar gesukkel met een jakkals wat ek drie keer misgeskiet het. Omdat sy elke keer op 4, 500 meter vir my net nie kans gee nie. En daai jakkals het vir my ore aangesit. At Oom Jan Toon’s farm Langplaas, I struggled for almost two years with a jackal that I missed on three occasions, because every time, at 400, 500 metres she did not give me an opportunity. And that jackal taught me a lesson. LINK Farming is about a lot more than a love of the land. This is how farmers put food on the table and send their kids to school… and like most of us they’ll do whatever it takes to protect their livelihoods JOHANNES Ons wil nie hê die jakkals moet uitsterf nie, gladnie. Die jakkals het net soveel reg soos ek om hier te wees. Maar die jakkals moet in sy area wees en ek moet in my area wees. Sodat ons kan altwee lewe… We don’t want the jackal to go extinct. Not at all. The jackal has just as much right as me to be here. But the jackal must stay in his area and I must be in my area, so that we can both live. Mac: Have you tried any other methods to get rid of them? Ja, ek het vir my anatoliese herdershonde gekry en dit werk relatief goed, en nou saans moet ek my skape op hok laat slaap, ek kan hulle nooit in die veld laat slaap nie. Yes, I got Anatolian sheepdogs and that works relatively well, and then at night I must let my sheep sleep in an enclosure. I can never let them sleep in the veld. V/O And although some of these mitigation measures help, Johannes maintains there are simply too many jackals. LINK Jackals are not just a problem for farmers in Olifantshoek. Even here, 700kms away and in a totally different environment … same issues! MEISIE Ons kry nie geboer saam met die jakkalse nie. Ek sê sommer hulle vreet ons oes op. We cannot farm with the jackals. I say, they eat our entire harvest. V/O Meisie and Danie Engelbrecht farm in Namaqualand…. With the expansion of conservation land to draw tourism to the area, they are struggling to cope with the thriving jackal population… and they are losing sheep on a weekly basis. MEISIE ‘N Boer se hart kan daai nie hanteer nie. Dis baie erg. Met hierdie droogte jare, dis al inkomste wat ons het. Ons lammeroeste is minder want ons ooie het gevrek van die droogte en dan kom die jakkals en dan kom vang hy …ag manne met meer skape dis maklik sommer ‘n klomp in ‘n nag. A farmer’s heart cannot handle that. It’s very bad. With these years of drought that is all the income we have. Our lamb harvests are less because our ewes died from the drought… V/O Here, herding the sheep to a kraal at night is not an option - the farm is just too vast and grazing too little… MEISIE Dan moet jy voer koop. Jy moet oor hierdie sleg pad met jou bakkie moet jy voer aanry van Springbok af wat peperduur is. Ons kan dit nie bekostig nie. Then you must buy feed. On this bad road, with your bakkie, you must transport feed from Springbok, which is very expensive. We can’t afford that. V/O They also cannot afford the additional labour, or to electrify their fences… MEISIE Mac: So, hoe maak julle? Hoe maak ons nou? Gee raad asseblief… So, what do you do? What should we do? Give advice, please. V/O Although Meisie says they do not kill the jackals on this farm, Danie the Jackal hunter has spent many nights on the West Coast plains … DANIE In die Weskus het ek normaalweg een elke drie aande geskiet - gemiddeld. En die meeste wat ek in een aand geskiet het was 7 jakkalse… On the West Coast I normally shot one every three nights on average. And the most that I shot in one evening was seven jackals. V/O As the sun begins to draw water it is time for the final preparations… DANIE Ek het sommer ‘n mobile bord wat ek opstel met pale… I have a mobile board that I put up with poles… V/O Danie uses a high caliber Winchester rifle with a telescope and rangefinder - specifically designed for varmint and big game. DANIE Mac: Gaan jy ons waarsky voor jy ‘n skoot vat. Ek gaan. Defnitief. Mac: Baie dankie Hy Het darem ‘n silencer… so hy sal nie ‘n baie harde klap geluid maak nie… Will you warn us before you take a shot? I Will, definitely. Thank you very much. It does at least have a silencer, so it won't make a loud noise. SHOT V/O (**Snigger) I was not quite as prepared for that, as I thought… V/O Satisfied with the calibration results, the rifle and lights are mounted on the vehicle…. And just as we set off, Johannes brings us a lamb carcass he just found near the road. JOHANNES Hierdie is ‘n extreme geval. Gewoonlik eet hy minder. Hier kan jy sien hy het tot sy ribbes regdeur afgebyt, sy bene uitgebreek. Alles opgevreet… This is an extreme incident. Normally it eats less. Here you can see it even bit right through its ribs, broke the bones. Everything is eaten. V/O We set off to find the culprit, before it does more damage. MAC UPSOUND So the hunt is now seriously on. There’s a searchlight doing the rounds, and hoping that we might catch a jackal’s eyes. DANIE Okay - woaw! Sit die rooi ligte af. Haal jou voet van die briek af… UPSOUND I can hear them… SHOT MAC That sound was loud. And it just came out of nowhere. I think that was the scariest part of it all. When you’re sitting in pitch black darkness, in the middle of no-where and you just hear that shot…. My heart almost stopped… DANIE As jy ‘n jakkals geskiet het, jy kry satisfaksie. Dit is satisfaksie wat jy gee omdat jy jou werk reg gedoen het. Hy het ‘n reg om te lewe. Hy het ‘n rego m te lewe want ons het in sy gebied ingetree met ons boerdery. Maar ongelukkig, in elke divisie van werk en sport is daar besering, en ongelukkig is die jakkals ‘n plaag. En ‘n probleem… When you’ve shot a jackal you get satisfaction. It is satisfaction that you give because you did your job right. It does have a right to live. It has a right to live because it is us who moved into his territory with our farming. But unfortunately, in every division of work and sport there is injury, and unfortunately jackal are a plague and a problem. PROMO 1 11” Across the Northern Cape, farmers are pitched against jackals in a battle to survive… Often hard choices have to be made but for some the answer is clear cut… PROMO 2 21” Hunting a jackal at 200 metres in the dead of night takes a sharp eye and a lot of patience. UPSOUND: Trees, thick bush… and still spot a jackal’s eyes… nah! PROMO 3 21” Farmers and jackals compete for land… and livestock… UPSOUND: ‘n Boer se hart kan daai nie hanteer nie. Dis baie erg. For some there is only one way to stop the onslaught… UPSOUND: Teen 3050 voet per sekond gee dit vir jou genoeg trefkrag om jou eerste skoot ‘n doodskoot te gee.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Farmers are resorting to hunting Jackals in the Northern Cape to protect their dwindling sheep numbers
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Seven years of drought means that most sheep farmers are down to 30% of their livestock carrying capacity in the Northern Cape. Even with recent rains it will take years for livestock numbers to recover and farmers are desperate. But the one animal that was not so much affected by the drought is the Jackal. Over the past decade their numbers have exploded and with a lack of apex predators keeping them in check, and the fact that food is still in abundance, the livestock farmers are suffering. For years many farmers have resorted to taking out jackals, calling them vermin and pests. There are even hunters specialising in Jackals. They are hired to take out entire families of Jackals to protect farmers' livelihoods. We have been invited to accompany a Jackal hunt and see the problem facing the farmers, first hand.
metadata.Summary: Human-Carnivore conflict is nothing new, but it is escalating across the continent as wild habitats decrease and human encroaching increases. Many Environmental NGO's run programmes, working with farmers when it comes to predator control. Various non-lethal deterrent methods exist, but in the forgotten areas of the Northern Cape - Namaqualand, farmers are faced with many problems. Electrified fencing, and even so-called Jackal proof mesh fencing is expensive and many cannot afford this. Jackals are clever and learn to dodge poison collars and dogs. There are even programmes that encourages farmers to play music, or ultra sonic sounds to keep predators away. Farmers will tell you that these are costly and largely ineffective. Many farmers choose to hunt Jackals - either themselves or they hire a professional to do the job.
metadata.Further information: There is very little you can farm with along the West Coast. Traditionally this has been sheep farming areas for many generations. With the drive to draw tourism to Namaqualand and the West Coast (Diamond Route) conservation areas are being expanded and the buffer zones that used to exist between wildlife and farmers are no more. Fences have been dropped and now every farm is a McDonalds for the Jackals and their numbers have exploded. Danie Du Plooy hunted Jackals for over 20 years. recently retired, he moved to Olifantshoek, but he has kept his records. it was his mission to understand Jackals, how they breed and their hunting and feeding habits. He says that hunting lone jackals have very little value, since another family will simply move into the territory, or the pups will simply grow and take over the area... To have any real effect, entire families need to be taken out and it's not easy to shoot a Jackal pup. Farmer Willie van Dyk farms with Sheep just outside Kleinzee on the West Coast. He put up electric fencing at a huge cost, but it only helped for a while. Soon the Jackals learned to dig under the fence and the stock losses continued. Fed up, he decided to start hunting Jackals and will take us on a hunt... Van Dyk's neighbour was so despondent about his losses that he sold his sheep, opting for goats.he believed that goats are not on the Jackal menu. He was wrong. Last week Jackals caught and ate 7 of his goats in one evening! As far back as 1922, the jackal was declared a pest, and an “evil to be reckoned with”. (According to the Journal of the Dept of Agriculture - Sept 1922). Black-backed jackal were controlled intensely with over 350 000 animals reportedly killed in the Cape Province from 1889 - 1908… In the past, the South African government subsidised farmers with predator control methods which mostly included lethal control such as the use of indiscriminate traps. This had very little negative effect on black-backed jackal populations, but a potential increased loss of other mammalian species (non-target species) and biodiversity has been observed on farmlands. But, since the 1990’s government no longer supports the control of Jackals and since the mid-2010’s farmers have been reporting an increase in Jackal numbers and predation on their livestock. Additionally, other apex predators numbers have fallen. An abundance of lions and leopards would have helped to keep jackal numbers down…
